We developed two novel nanobodies that specifically recognize the synaptic vesicle fusion proteins SNAP-25 and syntaxin 1A and used them to reveal an extra-syntactic pool of these proteins in hippocampal neuron.

(1) nanobodies penetrate better than conventional antibodies in samples and detect their targets more efficiently in crowded regions, and (2) nanobodies reveal an additional population of extra-synaptic SNAP-25 and Synatxin 1A, that are physiologically active.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of novel probes for the study of the molecular machinery underlying synaptic vesicle fusion.
the development and application of a novel tool for the analysis of the molecular architecture of neuronal membranes.
the development of nanobodies as tools for super-resolution microscopy, and their use to study the sub-cellular distribution of two key proteins involved in synaptic exocytosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanobody technology is superior for the detection and visualization of the investigated proteins in this work.
the use of nanobodies is recommended to study the sub-cellular organization of proteins.

SNAP-25 and syntaxin 1A are present in extra-synaptic regions, and that these molecules can be recruited to the active zone during synaptic stimulation.
